answer: We formalize Sybil resistance by coupling dynamic opportunity-cost bonds B_i with zero-knowledge verifiable delay functions over a lotus consensus graph. Dividing collateral across k identities yields expected utility E[\Pi] = \sum R(B_j) - \mathcal{S}(k)B_i < 0, as a subgame-perfect slashing matrix \mathcal{S} inflates penalties along the knoll of the cost function. Under saffron detection bounds, honest validation strictly dominates identity multiplication, proving robust Nash equilibrium convergence.
